title: You Really Didn’t Get That? Benchmarking Social Pragmatic Inference for Indirect and Playful Chinese Online Comments
one_sentence: A 4,735-item, human-validated Chinese-language social-pragmatics benchmark shows strong task-specific dependence on reconstructed interaction context while exposing unstable interpretations in a difficult revised subset.
problem: Can current language models recover the target, stance, wordplay mechanism, and interactional force of indirect or playful comments embedded in Chinese-language online interaction?
method: The authors purposefully sampled public interaction episodes from Zhihu, Tieba, Douban, and Xiaohongshu, screened more than 12,000 examples to retain 3,200 episodes, and generated 4,735 five-choice items with eight writer models and seven trained native-Chinese, high-frequency social-media users. They report three 200-item reliability audits, leave-writer-out solver accuracy, a random 300-item human audit, context ablations, and qualitative error cases.
findings: Across the tested model versions, reported leave-writer-out accuracy averaged 68.70%, while a random 300-item human audit reported 90.8% accuracy and kappa .85; these are not paired estimates on identical item sets.
Removing the reconstructed interaction context reduced mean model accuracy from 68.70% to 29.63%, a 39.07-point drop within this deliberately context-dependent benchmark.
The 343 human-revised difficult items produced only 64.14% human accuracy and kappa .53, revealing a meaningful ambiguity/gold-stability boundary.
real_contribution: Provides a native-language, multi-platform resource and a plausible-misreading diagnostic protocol for situated social meaning, moving beyond broad humor or sarcasm labels toward target, stance, mechanism, and interactional move.
biggest_weakness: Purposive selection conditions on context dependence, solver comparisons use different leave-writer-out item compositions, and adjudicated labels do not directly reveal original speaker intent or participant uptake.
claim_boundary: Supports context sensitivity within a purposefully sampled Chinese-language benchmark, not a claim about Chinese culture, all Chinese speakers, general cultural competence, dyadic common ground, or embodied adaptation.
why_researcher_should_care: It gives AMSC a rigorous upstream diagnostic template for social-meaning misreadings and a clear example of context-sensitive meaning that must not be mislabeled as common ground.
evidence_notes: Full arXiv HTML was inspected; exact values are preserved with their sampling and comparison boundaries.
Chinese denotes language and platform discourse ecology here, not a measured national or ethnic culture.
